name: PostCSS
one_liner: CSS transformation pipeline that most styling tools quietly run on.
what_it_is: A tool that parses CSS into an abstract syntax tree and applies plugins to it — most commonly Autoprefixer for vendor prefixes, and the plugins that implement Tailwind and similar frameworks.
why_it_matters: Most developers use PostCSS without knowing it, because it sits inside other tooling. Its direct relevance has narrowed as browsers implemented nesting and custom properties natively — a lot of what people used it for is now just CSS. Knowing it exists mainly helps when you need to debug what your build is doing to your stylesheets.
suitable_for: Autoprefixing for defined browser support targets
Tooling that builds on its plugin model
not_suitable_for: Projects that only wanted nesting or variables — the platform now provides both
